notes.meaning: Samuel served God faithfully at the tabernacle under the direction of Eli the high priest. In those days, God rarely spoke through prophets or visions because Israel had drifted away into sin and the priests were corrupt. Samuel's quiet obedience stood out like a bright light during this spiritually dark time.

Eli was growing very old, and his physical eyesight had become dim. His weak eyes also pictured the dull spiritual state of the priesthood at that time. Because Eli could not see to look after himself at night, Samuel slept near him to help him.

The golden lampstand in the sanctuary was kept burning through the night and was put out shortly before sunrise. This shows that the Lord called Samuel during the quiet early morning hours before dawn. Samuel was resting near the holy tent where the sacred chest called the ark of God was kept.
The Lord spoke out into the darkness and called Samuel by his name. Samuel answered right away to show that he was awake and ready to serve.
Samuel hurried straight to Eli's room, thinking the elderly priest had called for assistance. Eli told him that he had not called and instructed the boy to lie down again.

The Lord called Samuel's name a second time. Samuel got up and went to Eli again, completely certain that his master needed him. Eli spoke tenderly to him as a father would, but he sent him back to bed because he still did not understand what was happening.
Samuel loved and served the Lord, but he had never received direct prophecies from God before. Because God had not yet spoken to him in this special way, Samuel did not recognize the divine voice.

differ.view: Samuel was not yet spiritually converted or saved in his heart until this personal encounter with God.
Samuel already possessed genuine saving faith and spiritual knowledge of God, but had not yet received the public office or gift of prophetic revelation.

notes.meaning: The Lord called the young boy a third time, and Samuel once more ran to Eli to offer his help. Eli finally realized that it was the Lord himself speaking to the child, since no one else was present in the sanctuary.
Eli directed Samuel to go back to his bed and wait. He told him that if the voice called again, he should reply that he was listening as the Lord's humble servant.
The Lord drew near and called Samuel's name twice to show that this was a serious and loving moment. Samuel answered obediently, showing he was ready to hear whatever God wanted to say.

differ.view: The Lord standing there may have been a visible appearance of Jesus before His birth in Bethlehem.

notes.meaning: The Lord told Samuel that he was about to do something so shocking in Israel that it would stun everyone who heard about it. This warned of the tragic day when the ark would be captured by enemies and Eli's sons would die.
God promised that he would fully carry out every warning he had previously spoken against Eli's household. When the time of judgment arrived, God would not stop until it was completely finished.

God announced that Eli's family was being judged for sins that Eli knew all about. Eli's sons had treated holy offerings with open contempt and insulted God, yet Eli never used his authority as high priest to stop them or remove them from office.

The sins of Eli's household were so deliberate and defiant that no animal sacrifice or grain offering could ever turn away their earthly punishment. To be atoned for means to have sin covered and wiped clean by God. The high priesthood was permanently taken away from Eli's family line.

Samuel lay awake until morning, thinking about the terrible message he had heard. When dawn came, he quietly opened the doors of the sanctuary as part of his regular duties, afraid to tell the harsh vision to his beloved teacher.
Eli heard Samuel opening the doors and called him over with warmth, calling him 'my son.' Samuel answered right away, showing his continuous respect and readiness to serve the old priest.
Eli asked Samuel to tell him the Lord's entire message without hiding anything. He put Samuel under a strict oath, asking God to punish the boy severely if he held back a single word.

Samuel proved his honesty as God's messenger by telling Eli everything without softening the blow. Eli responded with quiet surrender, admitting that the Lord is the true King who has the right to do whatever is good in his sight.

differ.view: Some praise Eli's words as a model of humble submission to God's sovereignty, while others view his response as spiritual laziness because he never repented or pleaded for mercy.
Eli's humble acceptance of his punishment provides a comforting example for believers who must bow to God's will during times of severe grief.

notes.meaning: As Samuel grew into manhood, the Lord stayed close to him and filled him with wisdom. God made sure that every word Samuel spoke came true, proving that the young man truly spoke on God's behalf.

Across the entire country, from the northern city of Dan to the southern border of Beersheba, the whole nation recognized Samuel's calling. Because his prophecies never failed, everyone knew he was a true and trustworthy prophet of the Lord.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars observe that this is the first time the text gives Samuel the formal title of prophet, even though he had been performing priestly work without ever receiving the title of priest.

notes.meaning: The long period of spiritual silence was over, and the Lord continued to meet with his people at the tabernacle in Shiloh. God revealed his mind and will directly to Samuel, who then spoke God's message to all the people of Israel.
